addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	import AppKit
2	import Defaults
3	
4	/// An installed app that can open a workroom directory, offered in the detail toolbar's
5	/// "Open in…" menu. Only the supported editors that are actually installed appear.
6	struct ExternalEditor: Identifiable {
7	  let id: String  // bundle identifier
8	  let name: String
9	  let appURL: URL
10	
11	  /// Supported editors (bundle id + display name), in menu order.
12	  private static let supported: [(id: String, name: String)] = [
13	    ("com.microsoft.VSCode", "Visual Studio Code"),
14	    ("dev.zed.Zed", "Zed"),
15	    ("com.apple.dt.Xcode", "Xcode"),
16	  ]
17	
18	  /// The supported editors currently installed, resolved to their app bundle URLs. **Cached** — see
19	  /// `EditorCache`: this is read straight from `OpenInControl.body`, which since issue #139 renders
20	  /// once per visible workroom pane, so the uncached version's three LaunchServices lookups per
21	  /// evaluation would run per pane on every pane rebuild (including every frame of a split-divider
22	  /// drag). The cache drops on app launch/terminate, so installing an editor still shows up live.
23	  static var installed: [ExternalEditor] {
24	    EditorCache.shared.editors {
25	      supported.compactMap { editor in
26	        guard let url = NSWorkspace.shared.urlForApplication(withBundleIdentifier: editor.id) else {
27	          return nil
28	        }
29	        return ExternalEditor(id: editor.id, name: editor.name, appURL: url)
30	      }
31	    }
32	  }
33	
34	  /// The editor the primary "Open in" action uses: the one last picked (`Defaults[.lastEditor]`), else
35	  /// the first installed. nil when none are installed. Single source for the toolbar's open button, the
36	  /// ⌘O command, and the Go-menu item, so they always target the same editor.
37	  static var remembered: ExternalEditor? {
38	    let installed = installed
39	    return installed.first { $0.id == Defaults[.lastEditor] } ?? installed.first
40	  }
41	
42	  /// The editor configured for opening *file paths* (Settings → "Open file paths in",
43	  /// `Defaults[.filePathEditor]`), or nil when unset — i.e. the file's default app. Names the
44	  /// Changes-panel "Open file in…" action (issue #93). Unlike `remembered`, this never falls back to
45	  /// the first installed editor: an unset/uninstalled choice deliberately reads as "default app".
46	  static var forFilePaths: ExternalEditor? {
47	    let id = Defaults[.filePathEditor]
48	    return id.isEmpty ? nil : installed.first { $0.id == id }
49	  }
50	
51	  /// The app's Finder icon, sized for inline display beside its name in the
52	  /// "Open in…" button and menu. **Cached**, for the same reason `installed` is.
53	  ///
54	  /// Drawing into a fresh image rather than assigning `.size` on the returned one is load-bearing:
55	  /// `NSWorkspace.icon(forFile:)` may hand back an image from its own cache, so resizing it in place
56	  /// mutates shared state and every other caller silently gets a 20×20 icon.
57	  var icon: NSImage {
58	    EditorCache.shared.icon(for: id) {
59	      let source = NSWorkspace.shared.icon(forFile: appURL.path)
60	      return NSImage(size: NSSize(width: 20, height: 20), flipped: false) { rect in
61	        source.draw(in: rect)
62	        return true
63	      }
64	    }
65	  }
66	
67	  /// Open `path` (a workroom directory) in this editor.
68	  func open(_ path: String) {
69	    NSWorkspace.shared.open(
70	      [URL(fileURLWithPath: path)],
71	      withApplicationAt: appURL,
72	      configuration: NSWorkspace.OpenConfiguration()
73	    )
74	  }
75	}
76	
77	/// Memoizes the LaunchServices work behind `ExternalEditor.installed` / `.icon`, which are read from
78	/// SwiftUI view bodies — since issue #139 once per visible workroom pane, on every pane rebuild.
79	/// Uncached, one `OpenInControl` evaluation cost three `urlForApplication` lookups plus an
80	/// `icon(forFile:)`; a three-member split re-rendering per frame of a divider drag made that
81	/// hundreds of LaunchServices round-trips a second.
82	///
83	/// Invalidated when any app launches or quits, so installing (or deleting) an editor is picked up
84	/// without relaunching Workroom. Main-thread-confined in practice: every reader is a view body or a
85	/// menu builder, and the observers deliver on `.main`.
86	private final class EditorCache {
87	  static let shared = EditorCache()
88	
89	  private var cachedEditors: [ExternalEditor]?
90	  private var cachedIcons: [String: NSImage] = [:]
91	
92	  private init() {
93	    let center = NSWorkspace.shared.notificationCenter
94	    for name in [
95	      NSWorkspace.didLaunchApplicationNotification,
96	      NSWorkspace.didTerminateApplicationNotification,
97	    ] {
98	      center.addObserver(forName: name, object: nil, queue: .main) { [weak self] _ in
99	        self?.cachedEditors = nil
100	        self?.cachedIcons.removeAll()
101	      }
102	    }
103	  }
104	
105	  func editors(_ resolve: () -> [ExternalEditor]) -> [ExternalEditor] {
106	    if let cachedEditors { return cachedEditors }
107	    let resolved = resolve()
108	    cachedEditors = resolved
109	    return resolved
110	  }
111	
112	  func icon(for id: String, _ render: () -> NSImage) -> NSImage {
113	    if let cached = cachedIcons[id] { return cached }
114	    let rendered = render()
115	    cachedIcons[id] = rendered
116	    return rendered
117	  }
118	}

content.text:
Based on my analysis of the diff and full read of `ExternalEditor.swift`, this change is a UI restructuring around issue #139 that:

1. Moves per-target run/open-in controls from the window title bar to each workroom pane's own header
2. Adds a per-target overload `runOrFocusRunCommand(for:)` that acts on an explicit target (rather than the selection)
3. Adds an `EditorCache` singleton to memoize LaunchServices lookups (previously done many times per render)
4. Moves the "Directory not found" state from a `RootView` branch into `TargetTerminalDetail` so every visible pane (not just selected) gets the guard
5. Introduces a `WorkroomPaneToolbarPresentation` pure enum for the trailing-control matrix (with tests)
6. Live divider ratio kept in local `@State` and committed only on mouse-up

Security-relevant observations:

- **`runOrFocusRunCommand(for:)`** drops `isEditingTextField` — but this is intentional (comments explain the ambient shortcut retains its guard; button clicks carry their own target). The target still comes from UI-owned state; not attacker-influenceable.
- **`ExternalEditor.open`** uses `NSWorkspace.shared.open([URL(fileURLWithPath: path)], withApplicationAt:)` — no shell interpretation. `path` is a workroom directory the user already sees. `withApplicationAt` uses a bundle URL resolved from a hardcoded allowlist of bundle IDs.
- **`EditorCache`** memoizes public LaunchServices data (bundle URLs of hardcoded editors + rendered icons). Comment claims main-thread confined; observers deliver on `.main`. Even if a race occurred, the cached data is not security-critical (public app metadata). No lock is required for correctness of security-sensitive state.
- **`TargetTerminalDetail`** — the new `!target.isMissing` guard is a defense-in-depth improvement, blocking terminal mount over a deleted path for every pane, not just the selected one. Security-positive.
- No new sinks: no exec/subprocess, no SQL, no HTML rendering, no path traversal, no deserialization, no network. No changed authorization/policy checks. No log/telemetry changes involving sensitive data. No CI/hook/allowlist changes.

No security vulnerabilities identified.
